evidence: Read cold in the section 'When the adult role is not available yet'. The draft is 'So, I came up with the idea of constructing a bridge – a temporary fix – a borrowed adulthood, if I can put it that way. It’s made up of a number of familiar practices (such as modeling and supported action), even though I’m not claiming the whole sequence has been proven as one treatment.' FLOW: it follows directly from the paragraph before it. That paragraph ends on the baby-bird line (telling someone to just access their adult is like telling a baby bird to just fly), and 'So, I came up with the idea of constructing a bridge' is the natural next move: problem, then the fix. 'borrowed adulthood' echoes the 'forced adulthood' two sentences earlier and sets up the 'borrow' / 'borrowed figure' steps that follow, so the term is not left hanging. PRONOUNS AND REFERENTS: 'It’s made up of' points at the bridge / borrowed adulthood (the only candidate that can be 'made up of practices'; 'the idea' is the other grammatical candidate but cannot be composed of practices). 'the whole sequence' is anchored by 'familiar practices' just before it and is the steps the next paragraphs give (witness, borrow, put on the hat, return). The source has the same definite 'the whole sequence'. No naming problem (C01) and no pronoun pointing at the wrong thing (C02). MEANING AGAINST SOURCE.txt: both published points are present: the practices are familiar ones ('familiar practices (such as modeling and supported action)'), and he does not claim the whole sequence is proven as one treatment ('I’m not claiming the whole sequence has been proven as one treatment'). 'provisional' appears as 'temporary fix', which the section itself supports (heading says 'not available yet'; later 'Once you’ve found something good, try it, don’t keep doing the exercise'). 'author-developed' appears as 'I came up with the idea of constructing', which is the same authorship, not a new fact. The naming 'that I call' is softened to 'if I can put it that way', but that still marks the term as his own figure of speech. Dropping 'formally tested' leaves the same not-claiming. 'such as' keeps the practices a non-exhaustive sample, which is fine because the replaced words also gave only modeling and supported action. Nothing is added that the source does not have: no study, no person, no new first-person fact (C03, C04 absent). SMALL READING NOTES, none a fail: (1) 'even though' puts a concession where the source had 'but'. It reads as casual speech (the familiar parts sound established, even though he is not claiming the whole is proven) and the meaning is unmistakable. (2) The spaced en dashes are the only dashes anywhere in this section; there is no inventory row for them, and punctuation against his own texts is the Emulate check's job, not a tell row here. TELL ROWS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the literal draft in its context and found none actually happening. Closest calls: T07, where 'if I can put it that way' is a hedge on his own coined phrase inside a sentence, a real thought-turn about an odd metaphor and not a stage direction between beats. T15, where the second sentence keeps the replaced sentence's skeleton, but that skeleton is the two published points that have to stay, the reused phrases are the exempted kind, and the swaps (built from to made up of, like to such as, but to even though, suggesting to claiming) are plain words, not rarer ones. T17, see B1 below. T13 and T09, see D9 below. LINTER FINDINGS: (a) 'B1 finished principle', flagged on 'It’s made up of a number of familiar practices (such as modeling and supported action), even though I’m not claiming the whole sequence has been proven as one t'. Not a real problem here. The sentence is a caveat about this one sequence and its provenance, not a general aphorism of the 'X can be Y and still Z' kind, and it is his published point (without claiming the complete sequence has been validated). Accepted. (b) 'D9 follows the source order', 1 of 1 paragraphs. With a two-sentence paragraph whose job is to name the bridge and then say what it is made of and what is not claimed, the order is dictated by sense (name the thing before describing it). The paragraph does notice things on the way ('if I can put it that way' acknowledges the figure; the concession states the limit of the claim). Accepted. Verdict PASS: it does what the_change says, keeps the source meaning, adds nothing, carries no unjustified tell, and reads right where it sits.
